thread:
Maria G: quick q — we need a final pass on span attribute keys before the exporter cut tomorrow. main concerns: model naming, token counts, and kvcache hits as ints vs bools.

Jon R: nailed it. my vote: stable prefix + descriptive key, e.g. `redwood.llm.model.name`, `redwood.llm.model.variant`. fewer surprises for downstream parsers.

Priya S: agreed. also we should avoid embedding full model config JSON in attrs — too big. keep a model_id that maps in the config service.

Sam B: about tokens — do we store `tokens.prompt`, `tokens.completion`, and `tokens.total`? or flatten with `redwood.llm.tokens.*`? queries from billing want per-stage counts.

Maria G: prefer namespaced: `redwood.llm.tokens.prompt`, `redwood.llm.tokens.completion`, `redwood.llm.tokens.total`. consistent with other metrics.

Jon R: and types: ints for counts, yes. but beware OTEL baggage size limits. best to emit counts on spans only for sampled traces or aggregated metrics pipeline.

Priya S: export pipeline: we have two paths — traces -> jaeger/tempo and metrics -> prometheus via collectors. For billing we need token counts ingested as metrics not just span attrs. so plan: span attrs include counts as ints but we also emit a counter metric aggregated in the collector.

Sam B: +1. that avoids retention blowup in trace storage. we should add a sampling hook that always keeps spans flagged as `redwood.llm.trace.important` when they cross error or quality thresholds.

Maria G: kv-cache hits — do we record `redwood.llm.kv_cache.hits` (int) and `redwood.llm.kv_cache.hit_ratio` (float) on the span? or only emit hit boolean for quick routing dashboards?

Jon R: emit hits as ints; hit_ratio can be derived later. boolean is lossy in our telemetry, and dashboards often want absolute counts.

Priya S: security/PII check: tokens are numeric only, not text, right? confirm we never attach prompt text or user messages to spans.

Sam B: yes — token counts only. any string fields must be whitelisted: model ids, region, route name. no prompt content anywhere. infra-bot: export job queued -> exporters: tempo, otlp-metric-aggregator. ETA 30m.

Maria G: thanks infra-bot. last bit: span naming. can we standardize to `llm.request` for top-level and add `redwood.llm.op` attribute for op like `generate`, `embed`, `rerank`? that keeps span names simple in traces/dashboards.

Jon R: i like that. sample span header:```
span.name = "llm.request"
attributes = {
  "redwood.llm.op": "generate",
  "redwood.llm.model.id": "rw-3b-v2",
  "redwood.llm.model.variant": "q8_0",
  "redwood.llm.tokens.prompt": 34,
  "redwood.llm.tokens.completion": 120,
  "redwood.llm.tokens.total": 154,
  "redwood.llm.kv_cache.hits": 1,
  "redwood.llm.route": "fast-us-west",
  "redwood.llm.trace.important": true
}```

Priya S: also add `redwood.inference.instance_type` (e.g. a100, h200) to help perf dashboards. keep everything snake_case under prefix.

Sam B: retention note: full traces -> 30d, sampled important -> 90d, metrics -> 400d. confirm with compliance?

Maria G: i'll ping legal for retention ok. for now please update the exporter config PR with the key names and the metric emission plan. I'll review after lunch. :thumbsup:

Jon R: working on PR now — will include collector filter that turns span counts into metrics and drops prompt-related attrs.

Priya S: once PR is up i can wire dashboards in console (tokens per model, kv cache hit heatmap).

infra-bot: exporter run started (id: exp-202103-9). logs -> https://logs.internal/redwood/exp-202103-9

Sam B: thanks all, big step. short follow-up: can we add a lightweight lint rule in otel SDK to enforce allowed attr keys? would save time.

Maria G: good idea — add it to the PR checklist. closing here once PR merged.
